title: First transcontinental railroad completed
summary: The Central Pacific and Union Pacific lines were joined at Promontory Summit, Utah, on 10 May 1869. Central Pacific construction began with a ceremony at Sacramento on 8 January 1863; the Union Pacific held its groundbreaking at Omaha on 2 December 1863, and track laying began in July 1865. The combined track ran 1,912 miles. Chinese laborers made up over 80 percent of the Central Pacific workforce.

uncertainty.note: Start is the Central Pacific groundbreaking at Sacramento (8 January 1863); end is the last-spike ceremony. The Union Pacific groundbreaking was 2 December 1863; most Union Pacific construction began with track laying in July 1865.

beats.caption: Central Pacific construction begins with a ceremony at Sacramento; the Union Pacific breaks ground at Omaha in December 1863.
Union Pacific track laying begins in July 1865 after financing problems and a Civil War labour shortage delayed work.
The rails meet at Promontory Summit on 10 May 1869, joining the lines into one railroad of 1,912 miles.

reviewer_note: Path waypoints are in date order, so the drawn line runs Sacramento, Omaha, Promontory Summit, not the two builders' separate routes. The 1,912-mile figure is combined track as the Census page gives it. Promontory pin is the GeoNames gap point. Waypoints ordered west to east (the two companies built toward each other), so the route is drawn static rather than growing by date.
